plan: SAT R&W batch 60: 8 new items on new passages CLD-P-SAT-RW-000536..000543 (critic-versus-author word choice, honeyguide control-condition inference, proportional-change table, a-number-of agreement). Difficulty provisional.

passages.title: Broad terms
passages.text: Some historians have criticized the treaty's language as ______, but its drafters chose broad terms deliberately, so that later governments could apply the agreement to circumstances that no one at the negotiating table could foresee.

passages.title: A partner in the hunt
passages.text: In parts of Mozambique, Yao honey hunters seek out wild bees' nests with the help of the greater honeyguide, a bird that leads people to nests and then eats the wax left behind after the hunters remove the honey. Hunters attract honeyguides with a special call, a trill followed by a grunt. When researchers played recordings of this call, of other human sounds, and of the calls of another bird species, honeyguides were far more likely to begin guiding in response to the hunters' call. This finding suggests that the honeyguides ______

passages.title: Reef fish
passages.text:
A team counted fish at reef sites where fishing is banned and at nearby sites where fishing is allowed.
Site type | Fish counted per survey, 2015 | Fish counted per survey, 2022
Protected | 120 | 210
Fished | 80 | 110
The team claims that protected sites gained more fish not only in number but also in proportion to how many they started with.

passages.title: Early photographers
passages.text: In the decades after photography was introduced in 1839, a number of early photographers ______ their chemical recipes secret, fearing that rivals would copy their methods.

passages.title: Training a rescue dog
passages.text: Having practiced the search routine dozens of times in empty fields, ______

passages.title: A mixed result
passages.text: The trial's results were ______: they showed that the drug reduced symptoms in most patients, but they also showed that the benefit faded within a few weeks of starting treatment.

passages.title: A fast library
passages.text: Searching a printed library catalog once required walking between drawers of index cards. ______ a reader can now search an online catalog in seconds from anywhere with an internet connection.

passages.title: One of a kind
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The daguerreotype was one of the first practical photographic processes.
- It was announced in France in 1839.
- Each image was formed directly on a polished, silver-coated copper plate.
- The process produced no negative.
- As a result, each daguerreotype was a single, unique image that could not be reproduced from the original plate.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: its drafters chose broad terms deliberately
candidates.explanation: The historians "criticized" the language, so their word must be negative and about broadness: "vague." The drafters reframe the same broadness as deliberate.

A.rationale: "Flexible" describes the drafters' positive intention, not the historians' criticism.

C.rationale: "Belligerent" means hostile, which has nothing to do with broad wording.

D.rationale: "Verbose" means wordy, but the issue is broad terms, not too many words.

hints: Is the blank the critics' word or the drafters'?

strategy.explanation: Predict a critical word for "too broad."

candidates.remember: Match the blank to the speaker it belongs to.

candidates.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: respond in the same way to any loud sound that people make in the forest.
choices.B: prefer the taste of honey to the taste of wax.
choices.C: can locate bees' nests only when hunters are nearby.
choices.D: treat the hunters' call as a specific signal to start guiding people.

candidates.evidence: far more likely to begin guiding in response to the hunters' call
candidates.explanation: Because the birds responded more to the specific hunting call than to other human sounds or other birds' calls, they appear to recognize that call as a specific signal.

A.rationale: The birds responded far more to the hunters' call than to other human sounds.

B.rationale: The text says the birds eat the wax; it does not compare their preferences.

C.rationale: The text says the birds lead people to nests, so they can find nests on their own.

hints: What did the comparison sounds rule out?

strategy.explanation: Ask why the researchers played other sounds.

candidates.remember: Control conditions show what a response is specific to.

candidates.stem: Which choice best uses data from the table to support the team's claim?

choices.A: Protected sites gained 90 fish per survey, while fished sites gained 30.
choices.B: In 2022, protected sites had almost twice as many fish per survey as fished sites.
choices.C: Protected sites rose by 75 percent, while fished sites rose by about 38 percent.
choices.D: Both protected sites and fished sites had more fish per survey in 2022 than in 2015.

candidates.evidence: in proportion to how many they started with
candidates.explanation: Protected sites went from 120 to 210, a 75 percent increase; fished sites went from 80 to 110, a 37.5 percent increase. Only choice C compares the proportional changes.

A.rationale: This shows a larger gain in number but not in proportion.

B.rationale: This compares the sites in one year; it does not show how much each changed.

D.rationale: This shows that both increased but does not compare the increases.

hints: What does "in proportion" require you to compute?

strategy.explanation: Compute percent change for each site type.

candidates.remember: A claim about proportion needs percent change, not raw change.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.explanation: "A number of" (meaning several) takes a plural verb, and the past tense fits "In the decades after ... 1839": "kept."

B.rationale: "A number of" means "several" and takes a plural verb; "keeps" is singular and present tense.

C.rationale: "Has" is singular and does not agree with the plural sense of "a number of photographers."

D.rationale: "Was" is singular and does not agree with the plural subject.

hints: Does "a number of" mean one thing or many?

strategy.explanation: Compare "a number of" with "the number of."

candidates.remember: "A number of" is plural; "the number of" is singular.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: the hidden volunteer was found by the dog in under two minutes.
choices.B: it took the dog under two minutes to find the hidden volunteer.
choices.C: the dog found the hidden volunteer in under two minutes.
choices.D: the volunteer's hiding place was found by the dog in under two minutes.

candidates.explanation: The one who practiced the routine is the dog, so "the dog" must come right after the opening phrase.

A.rationale: The opening phrase would describe the volunteer, who did not practice the routine.

B.rationale: The opening phrase would describe "it," not the dog.

D.rationale: The opening phrase would describe the hiding place.

strategy.explanation: Put the doer right after the comma.

candidates.remember: An opening modifier describes the noun that follows it.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: but they also showed that the benefit faded
candidates.explanation: The results were good in one respect and limited in another, so "mixed" fits.

A.rationale: "Conclusive" suggests the results settled the question, but they point in two directions.

B.rationale: The results were partly encouraging, so "disappointing" captures only half of them.

C.rationale: Nothing suggests the results had never been seen before.

hints: Are the results all good, all bad, or both?

strategy.explanation: Predict a word for "partly good, partly bad."

candidates.remember: Use "but" to see that the explanation has two sides.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
candidates.evidence: a reader can now search an online catalog in seconds
candidates.explanation: The second sentence contrasts the modern method with the old one, so "By contrast" fits.

A.rationale: Searching online is not an example of walking between drawers.

C.rationale: The online search is unlike the old method, not similar to it.

D.rationale: Walking between drawers did not cause online searching to exist.

hints: How do the two sentences relate?

strategy.explanation: Label the relationship before reading choices.

candidates.remember: Use a contrast transition for then-versus-now comparisons.

candidates.stem: The student wants to emphasize a limitation of the daguerreotype process. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Because the daguerreotype process made no negative, each image was unique and could not be reproduced.
choices.B: The daguerreotype, announced in France in 1839, was one of the first practical photographic processes.
choices.C: Each daguerreotype image was formed directly on a polished, silver-coated copper plate.
choices.D: Announced in 1839, the daguerreotype formed images on polished, silver-coated copper plates.

candidates.evidence: could not be reproduced from the original plate
candidates.explanation: The limitation is that, with no negative, each image could not be reproduced. Only choice A states it.

B.rationale: This gives the date and importance, not a limitation.

C.rationale: This describes the method but does not state a limitation.

D.rationale: This combines the date and method but omits the limitation.

hints: Which choice names something the process could not do?

strategy.explanation: Check each choice against the goal.

candidates.remember: A synthesis answer must accomplish the stated goal.
